# A clean fragment

Anna left the house at quarter past seven, her grey umbrella tucked under one arm. Nikolskaya Street was empty. Even the cleaners had not yet started their rounds. The metro stood three hundred and fifty metres away, and she walked slowly, counting steps, the way her grandmother had taught her.

At the corner she stopped. There was no reason to stop, except that the morning was cold and the coffee shop smelled of burning sugar — the beans were roasting later than they should have been. She watched the roaster turn for a moment, then walked on. The umbrella stayed closed. The rain held off until she reached the station.

Her brother had arrived from St Petersburg the night before. He would be waiting at the cafe by the metro, reading a newspaper. He always read newspapers in cafes. The habit irritated her, and she had told him so years ago, and he had not changed.
